title: CE351 : NUMERICAL METHODS
description: Matrix Algebra reviewer divided into two focused topics.

topics.title: MATRIX ALGEBRA  -  PART 1
topics.description: Matrices, notation, equality, operations, properties, and matrix multiplication.

content.text: A matrix is a rectangular array of numbers or functions. An entry is written as aij, where i identifies the row and j identifies the column.
The size of a matrix is written m × n, with m rows and n columns. A row vector has one row; a column vector has one column.

content.explanation: The array has 2 rows and 3 columns, so its dimension is 2 × 3.

content.text: Two matrices are equal when they have the same size and every corresponding entry is equal.

content.title: Equality of matrices
content.expression: A = B  when  aᵢⱼ = bᵢⱼ for every i and j
where: A and B must have the same dimensions.
Every corresponding entry must be equal.

content.explanation: Equality compares entries in the same row and column position.

content.text: Matrices can be added only when they have the same dimensions. Add corresponding entries: (A + B)<sub>ij</sub> = a<sub>ij</sub> + b<sub>ij</sub>.

content.title: Matrix addition
where: A and B must have the same dimensions.

content.explanation: Each position is added to the entry in the same position.

content.text: To multiply a matrix by a scalar, multiply every entry by that scalar. For kA, (kA)<sub>ij</sub> = ka<sub>ij</sub>.

content.explanation: The scalar 2 is applied to all four entries.

content.title: Matrix operation properties
content.expression: A + B = B + A   |   (A + B) + C = A + (B + C)   |   k(A + B) = kA + kB

items: Matrix addition is commutative: A + B = B + A.
Matrix addition is associative: (A + B) + C = A + (B + C).
Scalar multiplication distributes over matrix addition: k(A + B) = kA + kB.
The zero matrix is the additive identity and the identity matrix is the multiplicative identity when dimensions permit.

content.explanation: These identities are rules to apply when simplifying matrix expressions.

content.text: The product AB exists when the number of columns of A equals the number of rows of B. If A is m × n and B is n × p, then AB is m × p.

content.title: Matrix multiplication
where: The number of columns of A must equal the number of rows of B.
Each entry is a row-by-column dot product.

content.text: Each product entry is the dot product of a row of A and a column of B: (AB)<sub>ij</sub> = Σ a<sub>ik</sub>b<sub>kj</sub>.

content.explanation: The 2 × 2 result is formed from row-by-column dot products.

content.text: For A = [[1, 2], [3, 4]] and B = [[5, 6], [7, 8]], AB = [[19, 22], [43, 50]]. Matrix multiplication is generally not commutative, so AB may differ from BA.

content.explanation: This worked example preserves the entries and products shown in the reviewer.

content.text: Practice identifying matrix dimensions, adding matrices, applying scalar multiplication, and calculating products. Show complete solutions.

topics.title: MATRIX ALGEBRA  -  PART 2
topics.description: Transposition, transpose rules, and special matrix classifications.

content.text: The transpose Aᵀ is formed by interchanging the rows and columns of A. The first row becomes the first column, and so on.
Transposition lets us work with a matrix or its transpose, whichever is more convenient.

content.explanation: The three rows of A become the three columns of Aᵀ.

content.text: A symmetric matrix is square and satisfies Aᵀ = A. Its entries mirror across the main diagonal.

content.title: Symmetric matrix
content.purpose: identifying a matrix whose entries mirror across the main diagonal.

content.explanation: The entries on opposite sides of the diagonal match.

content.text: A skew-symmetric matrix is square and satisfies Aᵀ = −A. Every diagonal entry of a skew-symmetric matrix is zero.

content.title: Skew-symmetric matrix
content.purpose: identifying a matrix whose transposed off-diagonal entries have opposite signs.

content.explanation: Transposing reverses the signs of the off-diagonal entries.

content.text: An upper triangular matrix has zero entries below the main diagonal. A lower triangular matrix has zero entries above the main diagonal. Strict triangular matrices also have zeros on the main diagonal.

content.title: Triangular matrices
content.expression: Upper: aᵢⱼ = 0 for i > j   |   Lower: aᵢⱼ = 0 for i < j

content.explanation: The zero regions identify whether a matrix is upper or lower triangular.

content.text: A diagonal matrix is square and has nonzero entries only on its main diagonal; all entries above and below it are zero.
A scalar matrix is a diagonal matrix whose diagonal entries are all equal to the same scalar.

content.explanation: Every diagonal entry equals 5, so this matrix is 5I.

content.text: A unit matrix, also called an identity matrix, is a diagonal matrix with 1s on the main diagonal and 0s elsewhere.

content.title: Unit matrix
content.purpose: serving as the multiplicative identity when dimensions permit.

content.explanation: Multiplying by I₃ leaves a compatible 3-component vector unchanged.
